summary: Record native sanlock and libvirt storage-lease checks in a disposable lab

guide.reason: This records contributor-run simulation results and adds no implemented operator workflow.

api.reason: No Core, Controller, or client API implementation or contract changed; native engine results do not implement Nex storage-lease status or promotion proof.

roadmap.reason: The report records native simulation results and leaves Core integration and the planned storage-lease acceptance gate open.

state.reason: Only a newly created disposable fixture was prepared and cleaned; no Nex pool or Controller record changed.

verification.method: Prepared an owned three-Core nested-QEMU fixture; hotplugged and verified emulated watchdogs; confirmed SBD inactive; installed Debian Trixie sanlock/libvirt packages only in the guests; configured separate dedicated NFS lease and VM-image exports; exercised local VM lease, duplicate shared-disk start, isolated sanlock authority-resource contention, watchdog reset with exact HOST_FAIL-to-HOST_DEAD observation, HOST_FREE, and generation change on rejoin. In a fresh disposable fixture, installed sanlock 3.9.5-1, libvirt 11.3.0-3+deb13u3 and QEMU 10.0.13+ds-0+deb13u1; mounted two private NFSv4 exports; configured explicit XML leases for separate lockspaces `repoa` and `repob`; observed ordered two-resource acquisition, same-key cross-host refusal, second-resource contention with first-resource rollback, retry success, and concurrent distinct resource files for two VMs on Repository A. Used raw shareable test disks to bypass QEMU's independent NFS advisory lock and isolate sanlock. `ReadSanlockHostStatus` returned HOST_LIVE for `repoa/1`, `repob/1` and `repob/2` (generation 1, io_timeout 10). The fixture cleanup command rejected Core QEMU paths recorded by a repo-relative launch, so exact PID/start-time/process-group/command ownership was revalidated before stopping recorded QEMU and VDE processes; the fixture-labelled container was removed. Only ignored cache artifacts remain. These are nested simulations, not physical watchdog, production NFS, Core integration or API evidence.
